scenes.line1: Why do logs fill up disks?
scenes.line2: And how do you stop it?
scenes.say: Why do logs fill up your disk, and how do you keep that from taking down your system?

scenes.label: /var/log
scenes.sub: System logs are in /var/log and the journal.
scenes.say: System logs live in slash var slash log, and in the journal. These are your first stop in any incident.

scenes.title: Handy log commands
scenes.say: Use journal control to see recent errors, tail to follow logs live, and dmesg to catch kernel events.
Logrotate keeps logs from filling your disk. It rotates, compresses, and deletes old files automatically.

scenes.question: Disk is full. What do you fix?
scenes.right: Fix logrotate or log level, not just the symptom.
scenes.say: If your disk fills up, don't just delete logs. Fix logrotate or reduce log levels, or the problem will come back.
